Building a Japanese clientele in US menswear retail

Language, cultural understanding and trust that brought customers back, with their friends.

The objective

Increase sales at a menswear retailer’s main store in downtown Chicago between 2011 and 2013, including by attracting the many international visitors drawn to the city by tourism and global events.

Raju’s contribution

Raju’s familiarity with different cultures and languages helped him serve the store’s international customers.

His ability to speak Japanese and understand the Japanese way of doing business built trust with Japanese visitors. One Japanese client returned the following year with friends, and this happened several times, gradually building a clientele of Japanese visitors whose purchases were larger than the store’s usual average.

The outcome

Several customers came to the store asking for Raju, and chose to wait for him when he was busy.

He was told that his sales contributed to an increase of approximately 19% in the store’s overall sales. The period and basis of that figure were not specified.

Source: Raju Lalwani’s account.

The experience this brings

Earning the trust of Japanese customers through language and cultural understanding, and turning that trust into referrals and repeat business.
